summary.one_liner: GPTSwarm is a Python library for building LLM-based agents as graphs and for organizing and optimizing swarms of such agents.
summary.what_it_does: GPTSwarm lets you construct LLM agents from graphs and compose agents into swarms that self-organize and self-improve. The library is split into modules: swarm.environment (domain operations, agents, tools, tasks), swarm.graph (creating and executing agent and swarm graphs), swarm.llm (selecting LLM backends and computing operational costs), swarm.memory (index-based memory), and swarm.optimizer (algorithms to improve agent and swarm performance). The README shows a predefined swarm run on the "gaia" benchmark setting with agent types such as "IO" and "TOT", and an example that passes a local image file to the swarm. Edge optimization adjusts inter-agent connection probabilities, pruning or creating edges to raise benchmark scores. Web search can be enabled through Bing, SearchAPI, or Google keys, selected in that priority order. A local LLM can be used via LM Studio.
use_cases: run multi-agent swarms on benchmark tasks
optimize agent graph edges for better scores
answer questions with web search-backed agents
summarize or analyze files such as images with an agent
run LLM agents against a local model via LM Studio
research on self-organizing language agent systems
how_to_run: conda create -n swarm python=3.10 && conda activate swarm
Add API keys to .env.template and rename it to .env
from swarm.graph.swarm import Swarm; swarm = Swarm(["IO", "IO", "IO"], "gaia"); answer = await swarm.arun({"task": "What is the capital of Jordan?"})
notable: Agents are defined as graphs, and inter-agent edges are optimized automatically toward better benchmark scores
Modular structure with separate environment, graph, LLM cost tracking, memory, and optimizer packages
Accompanies the ICML 2024 paper 'Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs' (oral presentation)
Supports a local LLM via LM Studio using model_name='lmstudio'
caveats: Setup requires Poetry and a conda environment, and API keys for the LLM and search backends
The README does not state a license
Local LLM support depends on running LM Studio separately
keywords: ai agent that searches the web
